name: Occasional One-Sided Getback of Singletons
proof: For $n=1$ the unique concept is known, so always predict its label and receive no mistake report. For $n\ge2$, fix any domain order and predict zero until the first mistake report. If it occurs at coordinate $i$, the target is necessarily the singleton $\{i\}$; thereafter predict that target exactly. Silence reveals no information and is ignored. This yields at most one reported mistake. Conversely, at the first coordinate $i$, both labels occur among singleton concepts. For either deterministic initial prediction, choose a target with the opposite label there and report that mistake. Thus every fixed order and prediction rule has worst-case cost at least one.
